input.quote: (d) Termination for Competing Product of Sanofi. If after [***]: (i) Sanofi or its Affiliates, alone or with or through a Third Party, develop, manufacture or commercialize a Competing Product and (ii) Sanofi or its Affiliates have not commenced a Registrational Clinical Trial for a Product prior to commencing the activities in Section 12.2(d)(i), RevMed may terminate this Agreement effective [***] after it delivers written notice to Sanofi that it is exercising its rights under this Section 12.2(d)
input.rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use covenant binds Sanofi anywhere in the Agreement, so the preferred position is met. The only exclusivity covenant runs the other way: § 3.5(a) prohibits RevMed (not Sanofi) from Researching, Developing or Commercializing SHP2 Inhibitor products outside the Collaboration, which benefits us. Sanofi's licence under § 3.1(a) is in the "Field," defined as "any and all uses," with no territory or indication limitation on our own programs, and the Article XIII covenants contain only RevMed-side undertakings. The competition-related provisions touching Sanofi are not restrictions on our business: § 12.2(d) merely gives RevMed a termination right (with a cure election) if Sanofi develops a Competing Product without having started a Registrational Clinical Trial for a Product, and the § 15.2 Acquiror/Acquired Party Family conditions are mutual firewall requirements attached to permitted assignment rather than a covenant not to compete. We note in passing that § 12.2(d) operates as a soft commercial disincentive to competing programs, but since it imposes no prohibition and no post-term restraint it does not engage this rule; no redline proposed.
